prompt: A fridge makes its inside colder. Why does this not violate the second law of thermodynamics?

options.text: Cold is not a form of energy
The fridge exports more entropy to the room than it removes
The second law applies only to gases
Electricity is exempt from the second law

explanation: The second law constrains the whole system, not one corner of it. The fridge lowers entropy inside by raising it more outside, which is why the back of a fridge is warm.
